title: 19.3 A Fractional-N PLL with 34fsrms Jitter and -255.5dB FoM Based on a Multipath Feedback Technique
problem: Advanced wireless communication (4K-QAM and beyond) requires frequency synthesizers with sub-100 fs RMS jitter to meet stringent phase-noise requirements. Prior fractional-N PLLs achieve excellent jitter but rely on impractically high reference frequencies (150–500 MHz), unsuitable for cost-effective deployment.
motivation: Mass-market wireless devices need low-cost, low-reference-frequency PLLs meeting modern modulation spectral purity; high reference frequencies increase BOM cost and power.
method: Multipath feedback technique in an analog PLL architecture enables competitive jitter performance despite low 80 MHz reference frequency (7.5x lower than prior sub-100 fs designs). The technique exploits parallel feedback paths to reduce charge-pump dead-zone and reference spur injection, improving phase margin and jitter. PLL operates 7.3–9.5 GHz output range.
key_novelty: Multipath feedback technique in analog PLL achieves 34 fs RMS jitter at practical 80 MHz reference frequency, eliminating need for expensive high-frequency references.
contributions: Fractional-N PLL with 34 fs RMS jitter and -255.5 dB FoM
Low 80 MHz reference frequency enables cost-effective deployment vs. 150–500 MHz prior art
Multipath feedback improves charge-pump efficiency and reduces reference spurs
Practical 7.3–9.5 GHz output range for modern wireless standards

metrics.other: Jitter 34 fs RMS, FoM -255.5 dB, frequency range 7.3–9.5 GHz

baselines: Prior fractional-N PLLs with 150–500 MHz reference frequency
limitations: Loop bandwidth, settling time, and process corner variation not discussed in abstract.
